inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-built: AU 10y govt ~4.2% + 5.5% ERP x beta ~1.35 (ASX small-cap consumer discretionary, mkt cap ~A$590m, no debt) = 11.5% cost of equity = WACC. Same rate in all three scenarios — cyclicality and Amazon/competition risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate (owner-fcf.md s7f).
notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (dcf-methods SKILL routing: operating company, consumer internet/marketplace), 10-year explicit horizon because margins are still ramping, component-built margins, scenario-weighted. Fresh build — no prior TPW.AX DCF.

OWNER FCF: last_fcf = reported FCF 14.055 − SBC 4.177 − interest income 4.847 − lease principal 6.615 = −1.584. Interest income is stripped because net cash (A$123m) is many times the FCF base and is added back in the bridge.

LEASES: treatment (B) — leases as operating cost. Lease cash (principal 6.6 + interest 1.9 in FY26; modelled at 1.8% of revenue because the liability doubled to A$42.4m on the Melbourne warehouse and payments step up) is charged inside the flows; lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt, so net debt = −cash = −122.694. D&A (0.5%) and capex (0.8%) are modelled ex-ROU (ROU depreciation was 11.4 of the 12.9 D&A).
EBITDA margin driver is on the reported post-AASB16 basis (comparable to the FY27 5-6% underlying guide) with the lease cost then deducted explicitly — do not read the 7.5% mature margin as pre-rent.

WORKING CAPITAL: FY2024-FY2025 OCF/FCF were inflated by negative-working-capital growth (FY2025 owner FCF A$27.4m vs NPAT A$11.3m); in FY2026 growth slowed and deferred revenue fell (27.8 -> 22.5), so the inflow collapsed. Modelled as a capture rate on the CHANGE in revenue (10% base), which turns into an outflow in the bear case decline.
GROSS MARGIN break: FY2023 onward includes shipping in COGS (~33%) vs ~45% before — presentational, not a margin collapse; the model works from EBITDA margin so it is unaffected.
TAX: 30% Australian statutory on EBIT (SBC is non-deductible, so cash tax on the SBC-expensed EBIT is close to statutory; FY26 cash tax A$3.6m on PBT A$11.9m).
PRICE is a regular close, not an after-hours print, but the stock is 7 days past a −16% result-day move and 80% below its 52-week high — expect volatility.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 10-year revenue CAGR (judgment). Equity CAGR is distorted by A$43m of buybacks over FY2024-26 and the owner-FCF CAGR is undefined (FY2026 owner FCF negative); revenue CAGR (15-19%) is the pre-slowdown figure and is not extrapolated.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5y CAGR 4.7% diverges >30% from revenue 5y CAGR 15.3% and EPS 5y CAGR −20.8%: revenue growth has not translated into per-share earnings or book value.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF − SBC − interest income − lease principal, applied to the whole history. Owner FCF fell from A$27.4m (FY2025) to −A$1.6m (FY2026) as the working-capital inflow stopped and capex rose (Melbourne warehouse fit-out); the reported series (−9% 3y CAGR) understates that decline. SBC has grown faster than cash flow: 1.0% of revenue in FY2019 to 0.6% in FY2026 on 6.5x revenue — modest by US standards.

scenario_narratives.base: FY27 revenue dips ~3% (first seven weeks −13% against a +28% comp, easing comps in H2, no revenue guidance), then re-accelerates to 8-10% as online penetration (~20% AU vs 29-35% UK/US), Home Improvement and Trade & Commercial compound; A$1bn revenue reached ~FY32, four years later than management's FY26-28 target. Post-AASB16 EBITDA margin 4.6% in FY27 (statutory, i.e. below the 5-6% underlying guide after NZ start-up and significant items), ramping 0.5pp/yr to a 7.5% mature level as marketing falls below 11% of revenue on the repeat-order mix. Lease cash cost 1.8% of revenue charged in the flows; 30% cash tax; 10% of the revenue increase captured as negative-working-capital inflow.
scenario_narratives.bull: The FY27 soft start is a comp artefact: revenue +3% in FY27 then 14-15% growth on faster online migration, Amazon failing to crack bulky-goods logistics, NZ and B2B scaling; A$1bn revenue by FY30. Exclusive/private-label mix (49% and rising) and AI conversion gains lift post-AASB16 EBITDA margin to 9% by FY32 — above anything TPW has yet delivered. Working-capital capture 12% of growth.
scenario_narratives.bear: The −13% opening is demand, not comps: cost-of-living pressure and housing turnover keep big-ticket discretionary spend weak, Amazon Australia and Kogan discount into the category, and marketing cannot be cut without losing share. Revenue −10% in FY27, flat FY28, then 3-4% — barely nominal GDP; EBITDA margin stuck at 3.0-4.5%. Negative-working-capital unwinds on the decline (capture 8% of a negative change), so owner FCF is negative in FY27 (−A$6.9m). Value is mostly the A$123m cash pile; no zero-floor hit but only A$1.39/share.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 rather than the house 15/50/35. Bear raised to 25%: FY27 opened with checkout revenue −13% and no revenue guidance, Amazon Australia is a live structural threat in a low-switching-cost category, and owner FCF was negative in FY26. Bull cut to 25%: it needs revenue to re-accelerate to mid-teens AND margins to reach 9% — two independent things going right — with no balance-sheet risk to offset (cash A$123m, no debt) but no scarcity either.
probability_weighted.band_note: Price A$4.82 sits above BOTH the house (A$3.51) and street (A$3.96) weighted values — band position 291% means the market is paying more than full non-cash-SBC credit would justify on these driver paths; the price implies the bull revenue path or a lower discount rate.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides; June FY-end monthly closes from Yahoo; net debt = -cash (leases excluded, consistent with treatment B). Will not match Yahoo GAAP P/E.
sanity_check.pe_test: NOT MEANINGFUL: FY2026 SBC-adjusted EPS is 0.1 cents (3.62c − 3.5c SBC/share) so implied and historical P/E are both degenerate (hundreds-to-thousands x). Test judged on P/B, EV/EBITDA and P/Sales instead.
sanity_check.diagnosis: No over-valuation: implied P/B 3.8x vs 10y max 28.4x; implied EV/EBITDA 15.8x vs 10y average 568x (ex-outliers; earnings near zero) and 30x at FY2026 close; implied P/Sales 0.61x is BELOW the 10y low of 0.99x. Base upside is −30% with price in the lower half of the 10y range. The DCF is more conservative than any multiple the market has paid.

valuation_philosophy: Owner-FCF DCF on strict owner economics: SBC expensed, interest income stripped, lease cash charged in the flows, working capital tied to growth not revenue. The history shows a business that grew revenue 6.5x since FY2019 while per-share earnings and owner FCF went nowhere — growth has been paid for in marketing (15% of revenue), rent and working-capital timing. The market has always valued TPW on revenue (P/Sales 1-5x) rather than cash flow, and at A$4.82 (0.9x sales, EV ~13x FY27 guided EBITDA) still pays for the A$1bn revenue and 5-6% margin story. The house model does not reject that story — the bull case at A$5.89 is roughly the price — but on a probability-weighted basis (A$3.51) and at a 15% hurdle (A$2.96) the stock is not yet a buy; the thesis is a margin re-rating, not a multi-bagger, and the entry price is where the bear case (A$1.39) stops being expensive.
